工厂运营最常用的五个数：节拍、瓶颈、OEE、在制品（Little 定律）、产线平: Five numbers commonly used in factory operations: cycle time, bottlenecks, OEE, WIP (Little's Law), and line balancing. In each lesson, calculate them by hand first, then find them in the simulation and change a parameter to see how the results change.
节拍：客户要多快: Cycle Time: How Fast Customers Need You to Produce
### 任务：算出节拍，再按节拍投料（约 15 分钟）\n\n**节拍**是客户:
### Task: Calculate the cycle time, then release parts at that rate (about 15 minutes)

**Cycle time** is determined by customer demand: "On average, how many seconds should pass between finished parts?"

> Cycle time = Available production time ÷ Demand

A bracket factory runs two 8-hour shifts per day, with a 30-minute meal break on each shift. The customer needs **900 brackets per day**.

The line has three operations: stamping M1 takes about 50 seconds, welding M2 about 55 seconds, and painting M3 about 45 seconds. Each is faster than the required cycle time, so the line should be able to meet demand. But parts are currently released using `expo(40)` (one part every 40 seconds on average), faster than the line can process them. The line-side buffer keeps growing, and a bracket can wait for several hours between release and storage.

1. Calculate the cycle time and enter it under "Targets and Answers" (enter the number only; the unit is seconds).
2. Select **Feed (SRC)** and set the **Arrival interval** under "Cycle Time" in the Properties panel to the calculated cycle time (enter a fixed number of seconds, for example, `75` for one part every 75 seconds).
3. Click "**Reset**" to clear the accumulated parts (when prompted, choose "Keep and Save" to retain your interval change), then run the simulation. Is the line-side buffer still accumulating parts? The targets are an hourly output of ≥ 58 parts and an average production cycle of ≤ 5 minutes.

> You may only change the feed interval. The processing times for the three operations represent equipment capacity and are used as given for grading.

#### Why learn this

Use cycle time as a reference when deciding how fast to release parts, how many shifts to schedule, and how many machines to use.
Releasing parts faster than the required cycle time only creates a growing queue on the line, taking up space and tying up capital while increasing lead time. Release them too slowly, and you won't meet demand.

间隔写成固定值（不带 expo），每件间隔一样，最不容易堆料。: Set a fixed interval (without expo) so every part arrives at the same interval. This minimizes buildup.

### 任务：找出瓶颈，改一个参数，让产量涨上去（约 20 分钟）\n\n整条线:
### Task: Find the bottleneck and change one parameter to increase output (about 20 min)

The number of parts the entire line can produce per hour is determined by **the slowest operation**. This operation is called the **bottleneck**.

The line-side inventory always has material available, but this line produces only about 48 parts per hour.

1. Run for at least 1 hour, then open "**Analysis**" → "**Time Breakdown**": Which machine spends the most time "Running" (green), with almost no time starved or blocked? Then check the three buffers: the buffer **before** the bottleneck is always full, while the one **after** it is always empty.
2. **Select the bottleneck machine** on the graph.
3. Answer: What happens to output if you speed up a machine that is not the bottleneck?
4. Change only the bottleneck machine's "**Parallel Workstations**" setting (under "Behavior" in the Properties panel; changing 1 to 2 adds an identical workstation operating in parallel). Run the model to verify: hourly output ≥ 65 parts.

> Do not change processing times. Changes to other machines' workstation counts do not count either (their original values will be used for grading).

#### Why learn this?

One of the most common forms of waste on the shop floor is putting effort into operations that are not the bottleneck. Speeding up an already fast machine only makes it become blocked sooner and builds up more WIP, without producing a single extra part.
Find the bottleneck first to make the best use of money and people.

OEE：设备到底干了多少活: OEE: How Much Work Is the Equipment Actually Doing?
### 任务：先手算 OEE，再在仿真里读、再把它提上去（约 20 分钟）\n\:
### Task: Calculate OEE by hand, read it in the simulation, then improve it (about 20 minutes)

**OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness)** = **Availability A** × **Performance P** × **Quality Q**

| | Calculation | Where the losses occur |
|---|---|---|
| A | Operating time ÷ planned time | Failures, changeovers |
| P | Actual output × ideal cycle time ÷ operating time | Waiting for materials, minor stops, slow speed |
| Q | Good parts ÷ actual output | Scrap, rework |

**Calculate by hand first**: A machine is scheduled for 480 minutes in one shift and has 60 minutes of downtime. Its ideal cycle time is 1 minute per part. It produces 350 parts, of which 340 are good.

**Then check the simulation**: This **#1 Press** has a 60-second cycle time, fails on average once every half hour, and takes 12 minutes to repair each time. About 6% of its parts also exceed the burr limit.

1. Calculate the OEE of the machine above by hand and enter it under
A = 420 ÷ 480，P = 350 × 1 ÷ 420，Q = 340: A = 420 ÷ 480, P = 350 × 1 ÷ 420, Q = 340 ÷ 350. Multiply all three together.
故障越频繁、修得越慢，A 越低。修复时间从 12 分钟降到 4 分钟，A 大约从: The more frequent the failures and the longer the repairs, the lower A becomes. Reducing repair time from 12 min to 4 min raises A from just over 70% to around 88%.
在「时间构成」表里，OEE 那一列就是 A × P × Q。: In the "Time Breakdown" table, the OEE column shows A × P × Q.

### 任务：把线上堆的料降下来，交期跟着缩短（约 20 分钟）\n\n**在制:
### Task: Reduce the material piling up on the line to shorten lead time (about 20 min)

**Work in process (WIP)**: Parts that have entered the line but are not yet complete. **Little's Law** describes a simple relationship:

> Average WIP = Throughput × Average production lead time

For example, if the line produces 60 parts per hour and the average WIP is 120 parts, each part takes an average of 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours from release to completion.

The warehouse delivers a large batch of **120 parts** to the line-side buffer every **2 hours**. That averages 60 parts per hour, which welding M2 (55 s) can handle, but once a batch is dumped into the line-side buffer, the parts behind it have to wait a long time.

每批 10 件、间隔 600 秒，每小时还是 60 件。: With 10 pcs per batch and a 600 s interval, the input is still 60 pcs/hour.

产线平衡：别让人闲着也别让人累死: Line Balancing: Keep Everyone Busy Without Overworking Them
### 任务：10 个人怎么分到 4 个工位（约 20 分钟）\n\n这是一条手:
### Task: How to Assign 10 People to 4 Workstations (About 20 Minutes)

This is a manual assembly line. The work at each workstation is fixed by the process:

| Workstation | Time per Part | People Now | If Each Person Works on a Whole Part, Average Time Between Parts at This Workstation |
|---|---|---|---|
| #1 Base Assembly S1 | 60 s | 3 | 60 ÷ 3 = 20 s |
| #2 Arm Assembly S2 | 120 s | 3 | 40 s |
| #3 Tightening S3 | 90 s | 2 | 45 s |
| #4 Labeling S4 | 30 s | 2 | 15 s |

The slowest workstation sets the output rate for the entire line (S3 here, at one part every 45 s, or 80 parts per hour). The operators at S1 and S4 spend half their time waiting.

**Line balance efficiency** = Sum of the times between parts at each workstation ÷ (Number of workstations × Time between parts at the slowest workstation). Higher efficiency means less idle time.

1. Calculate the current line balance efficiency and enter it under "Targets and Answers" as a percentage number. Mark the current slowest workstation on the diagram.
2. Keep the total at **10 people** and reassign them: select a workstation, then change **Parallel Workstations** (= number of people assigned to that workstation) under "Behavior" in the Properties panel. Target: output ≥ 110 parts per hour.
3. The "Investment" item under "Targets and Answers" in this lesson is based on **headcount** (1 per person). The total must not exceed 10.

> Do not change processing times; buffers do not count as people.

#### Why Learn This

Line balancing asks whether each workstation has roughly the same amount of work. On an unbalanced line, some people are rushed while others wait for parts. Everyone gets the same pay, but the busiest workstation limits the output of the entire line.
Assigning people according to workload can significantly increase output without changing the total headcount.
